title: Install Clew
summary: Install Clew under email admission maintenance, convert supported older ledgers transactionally, and preserve application history and daily scheduling.

consumers.statement: The authorized local installer and Cell deployment coordinator.

preconditions.statement: A validated committed candidate and compatible Cast, Email and Clockwork interfaces are available. Migration of a nonempty schema-one ledger also requires the Platter opportunity reader. Coordinated mutations require drained run-owned email maintenance; migration requires the sole owned hold.

inputs.statement: Use deploy.sh plan clew then deploy.sh clew from committed local main. The boolean daily_email_enabled setting changes daily intent; omission preserves it. Direct install accepts absolute --binary, --bundle and optional --home. schedule-definition requires existing state and a new absolute output file.

outputs.statement: The selected immutable release contains clew, clew-install, and the matching Chancery provider. Coordinated configure initializes empty schema-three state or converts schema one or two transactionally with retained exact retry requests and legacy aliases.

data_semantics.statement: Installation selects programs and initializes or migrates ledger state. It creates no new entries, statuses, or threads. Migration preserves entry IDs, times, sequence, text, corrections, retractions, and original write namespace. Existing jobs receive explicit application-report associations in the external reference model. Platter supplies only schema-one legacy-to-Cast mappings; schema-two conversion is local.

identity_and_units.statement: Content hashes identify immutable releases; package version, provider contract and database schema are separate identities.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installation performs setup without selected-byte integrity, local ledger integrity, or Cast snapshot checks. Migration retains its ordinary mapping requirements for every legacy reference. Installation establishes no future availability.

access.statement: The current user owns installation selectors and private ledger state.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The shared file transaction selects commands and provider atomically. Lifecycle captures, suspends, and drains email work, prepares the exact disabled definition, then restores intent after releasing its hold. Migration excludes ledger writers, commits schema three, reference associations, aliases, and exact write requests in one transaction. Old writers are rejected. Failure halts and frozen email bytes, keys, and receipts remain intact.

operational_limits.statement: There is no completion-time guarantee. Compatible schema-three readers and short SQLite writers can finish across program selection. Migration from schema one or two uses a separate guarded write boundary and preserves all retained entries atomically.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Only cell-install-v2 releases, ledger schema three, and email schema one are supported for ordinary use. Contract four supports guarded conversion from ledger schemas one and two. Ordinary commands and direct installation do not migrate state. Recovery requires a matching program and ledger pair; there is no automatic downgrade. Preserve email delivery records.

reliances.statement: Application features require the complete Cast snapshot reader for first-job admission, job search, and email context. Installation and generic ledger operations do not probe Cast.

Migration of a nonempty schema-one ledger reads retained Platter opportunities to map each legacy reference to its exact Cast job ID. Schema-two conversion and generic ledger operations do not read Platter.
Email submits the unchanged payload and stable key to the fixed recipient.
Clockwork activates the installed runner and enforces its shared service-health threshold before new scheduling failure halts.

use_when: Installing, checking or recovering the Clew command and private ledger.
do_not_use_when: Recording an application update or changing Platter preparation.
outcome: Installed Clew commands and provider, with coordinated state setup or migration.
effects: Program deployment selects immutable files and initializes a missing ledger or converts schema one or two to schema three under maintenance transactionally in place. Existing entry identity, content, and exact retry requests remain intact; no thread is invented.
The coordinator holds email admission and suspends scheduling while preparing the selected release. Activation restores captured or explicitly supplied intent without approving a halt.
authority: Clew owns its installation and ledger; the shared coordinator owns deployment ordering.
Clockwork owns schedule enforcement; enabling daily_email_enabled explicitly grants standing authority for the Clew digest.
success: Program selection, requested state setup, and maintenance release complete. Installation does not check artifact integrity, ledger integrity, or the Cast snapshot.
failure_and_recovery: File recovery preserves ledger state and must not claim an incompatible old program can operate schema three. Missing or colliding schema-one mappings stop the upgrade. Preserve current data and unresolved installation evidence. Unsupported or nonempty foreign state fails.
Retain email occurrences and uncertain acceptance across recovery. Resolve product and schedule selection before releasing run-owned admission; never erase or approve existing failure incidents.
privacy: Private ledger state is outside source and installation releases.
does_not_authorize: Adding application records, deleting history, immediate test mail, implicit first-time schedule enablement, or approval of a failure halt.
